description: Tag-lane declarations for the types a custom reader emits, which have no manifest entry to declare a `tags` block in (req-aws-collector-tags-14). One row per (entity type, reader). `tags` is either a manifest `tags_block` (validated against aws_resource_manifest.schema.json $defs/tags_block) or {"source": "organizations"}, the Organizations lane (req-aws-collector-tags-10): organizations:ListTagsForResource, shape list_kv, through normalize_tags and the tags_of unread sentinel in organizations.py. This file covers the Organizations reader (aws-core-tap#65) and the landing-zone reader (aws-core-tap#66); the registry-wide test over every emitting path is req-aws-collector-tags-14's (aws-core-tap#69).

lanes.why: The organization stands for its root, and organizations:TagResource accepts a root id (req-aws-core-organizations-completeness-1).
OU tags, organizations:ListTagsForResource on the ou- id.
Account tags set through Organizations stay on aws_account.tags (ruling 2026-10-01). The manifest's aws_account_singleton path declares owned_by under aws-core-tap#69.
Customer-managed SCP tags; an AWS-managed policy cannot be tagged and is written with {} without a call.
Customer-managed policy tags for every other policy type; an AWS-managed policy cannot be tagged and is written with {} without a call.

tags.why: AWS has no tagging operation for a delegated administration: it is a (member account, service principal) registration, not a resource.
A statement is part of a policy document, not an AWS resource; only the policy itself can be tagged.
A tag-policy rule is one key's entry in a tag policy document, not an AWS resource; only the policy itself can be tagged.
